content: {"summary":"In April 2025 the PAYAPI‑E1042 errors were caused by pgx connection pools on payments‑api‑03/‑04 filling to their 40‑connection ceiling due to long‑running queries, while in October 2025 the same error code appeared during a PgBouncer incident where the bouncer processes hit 100 % CPU but did not drop clients; failures still stemmed from the API timing out at its own deadline.","likely_cause":"April 2025 – pgx pool exhaustion from long‑running DB queries; October 2025 – PgBouncer CPU saturation causing API timeouts","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"April 2025 errors were due to pgx pools on payments‑api‑03 and ‑04 reaching their 40‑connection limit","evidence_ids":["INC-0035#0","INC-0035#2"],"quote":"pool full at 40 of 40"},{"text":"Long‑running queries on payments‑db‑01 kept connections busy, filling the pgx pools","evidence_ids":["INC-0035#2"],"quote":"long-running queries on payments-db-01 keep connections out"},{"text":"October 2025 errors involved PgBouncer processes (payments‑pgbouncer‑01/02) rather than pgx pools","evidence_ids":["INC-0095#0","INC-0026#1"],"quote":"Both payments-pgbouncer-01 and payments-pgbouncer-02 are involved"},{"text":"PgBouncer hit 100 % CPU but did not drop client connections; failures were API timeouts","evidence_ids":["INC-0055#3","INC-0026#1"],"quote":"no client was dropped by the bouncer; every failure was payments-api giving up at its own deadline"}],"next_checks":["Review pgx pool metrics and query durations for future incidents","Monitor PgBouncer CPU and connection counts during load spikes","Validate that API deadline (500 ms) aligns with downstream latency expectations","Confirm runbook RB-010 and RB-011 coverage for respective failure modes"]}
